title: Stitch and Spark: Quicklist coverage brief
body:
Purpose:
Quick lightweight tracker for ad-hoc coverage asks across eng/product/sales/CS while we triage the weekend surge plan. Not intended to be canonical — single-page scratchpad to hand off during standups and async updates.

Snapshot summary (as of 2026-03-22):
- Total open micro-asks: 7
- High-risk uncovered routes: 2 (EU ingest burst; Embeddings routing fallback)
- Estimated patch effort: ~6 engineer-days across teams

Tracker (rows = discrete ask / light analysis)
1) EU ingest fallback contact mapping | Owner: Liam O'Connor | Area: platform infra | Priority: P0 | ETA: 2026-03-23 | Status: in_progress | Notes: need region lead + networking owner; assign oncall if capacity spikes; related jira ENG-4572
2) Embedding route temporary quota lift | Owner: Priya Singh | Area: product-hosted-api | Priority: P1 | ETA: 2026-03-24 | Status: blocked | Notes: legal review required for cross-customer burst; CS customers impacted = 3 (acct-phi, acct-fin); ticket raised to billing (BILL-129)
3) Canary fallback variant mapping (gpt-ish -> quantized-compact) | Owner: Diego Ramos | Area: serving-runtime | Priority: P1 | ETA: 2026-03-25 | Status: todo | Notes: validate latency regressions, check KV cache warmup cost
4) Support play: canned responses and escalation ladder | Owner: Maya Chen | Area: customer-success | Priority: P2 | ETA: 2026-03-22 | Status: done | Notes: draft posted to #cs-ops; include links to status page and fallback instructions
5) Billing burnback quick-scan (estimate token delta) | Owner: Finance rotation | Area: finance-and-legal | Priority: P2 | ETA: 2026-03-26 | Status: todo | Notes: use last 72h baseline + +30% surge model; output by cost center
6) Lite observability sampler (top 5 slow routes) | Owner: SRE shift | Area: observability | Priority: P1 | ETA: 2026-03-23 | Status: in_progress | Notes: get traces for 95p latency > 800ms; attach sample traces to ENG-4572
7) Solutions eng: customer-impact reconciliation (who to contact) | Owner: Priya Singh | Area: solutions-engineering-and-professional-services | Priority: P2 | ETA: 2026-03-24 | Status: todo | Notes: produce 15-min customer note template

Quick decisions needed (open questions):
- Can we allow temporary quota bump for embeddings without updated TOS? (legal)
- Is EU fallback using cross-region routing acceptable for P0 customers? (security/network)
- Who owns postmortem if fallback triggers? (product vs platform)

Hand-off checklist (what to copy to final runbook):
- Links to tickets and traces (list above)
- Owner rotation for 48h window + backup contact (fill in when handoff happens)
- Short scripts for cache-warm and rollback steps (serving-runtime)
- Customer communication snippet and escalation numbers (CS + solutions)

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- If ENG-4572 hits > 3k req/min, toggle route B then rerun sampler.
- Keep one engineer on-call for the next 12h window to monitor coverage.
- Slack channel: #ops-stitch-spark (temporary) — add Liam, Priya, Diego, Maya.

Next sync cadence:
- 10:30 AM PST async update (post status + short bullets to channel)
- 2:00 PM PST quick triage if any P0 still open

Appendix: quick links and snippets to paste into tickets (copy/paste):
- "Observed: increased 95p latency on EU ingest between 02:00–03:00 UTC, fallback checks attempted but routing saturated. Immediate ask: map fallback contacts, consider temporary cross-region burst allowance."
- "Customer note template: \"We are aware of increased latency for request ingestion in EU regions. Our engineering team has deployed a temporary routing fallback and is monitoring. We expect mitigation within 24 hours; if you see persistent failures please contact support@redwood.ai with subject: EU-ingest-impact.\""

Design constraints / guardrails:
- Any temporary quota or routing change must be auditable; preserve logs and change tags.
- Avoid model downgrades that change output shape for client integrations unless approved by product owner.

Last quick log: 2026-03-22 09:44 PST — added SRE sampling request and pinged infra oncall.

End of brief.
